title: Adaptive Rehabilitation Robot
summary: A human-in-the-loop robotic platform that adapts assistance to each user's changing movement capability.
image_alt: Abstract placeholder for an adaptive rehabilitation robotics project
overview: This project studies how a rehabilitation robot can continuously adjust assistance as a user practices movement. The platform combines biomechanical sensing, interpretable adaptation, and therapist-informed constraints.
challenge: Recovery is highly individual and changes from session to session. A useful robot must provide enough support to enable practice while preserving the user's active contribution.
approach: We combine real-time movement features with human-in-the-loop control and structured evaluation protocols. The current placeholder can later be replaced with specific hardware, algorithms, datasets, and study details.

title: Variable-Stiffness Exosuit
summary: A lightweight wearable system exploring tunable compliance for safe and efficient physical assistance.
image_alt: Abstract placeholder for a variable-stiffness exosuit project
overview: This project explores a lightweight assistive exosuit whose mechanical compliance can be tuned to different activities and users.
challenge: Wearable robots need to deliver meaningful assistance without becoming heavy, restrictive, or uncomfortable during natural movement.
approach: We develop compact variable-stiffness mechanisms, characterize their mechanical behavior, and integrate them with wearable structures and low-level control.

title: Neural Intent Interface
summary: Multimodal sensing and learning methods for translating neural and biomechanical signals into assistive control.
image_alt: Abstract placeholder for a neural intent interface project
overview: This project investigates how neural, muscular, and biomechanical signals can be fused to infer movement intent for assistive robotic control.
challenge: Physiological signals are noisy and vary across users, sessions, and physical conditions, making robust real-time decoding difficult.
approach: We compare interpretable signal features and learning-based representations, then evaluate how reliably they support closed-loop interaction.
